title: Machine-coding problem bank (timed)
summary: Timed machine-coding problem bank (18 problems: LRU/TTL cache, rate limiter, parking lot, transactional KV, pub-sub, job scheduler, Splitwise, elevator, ticket booking, in-memory file system, async logger, vending machine, order book, inventory reservations, resilient HTTP client, URL shortener, plus two stretch problems and the round playbook), each with staged requirements, failing tests, a reference solution, a rubric and a debrief.

units.title: Caches and limiters: data structures, clocks and locks
Modelling and state: parking lot, transactions
Messaging and scheduling: acks, redelivery, timers
Trees and sinks: in-memory file system, async logging
State and matching: vending machine, order book
Reservations and resilience: inventory, HTTP client, URL shortener
Stretch problems and the round playbook

labs.title: LRU cache with TTL: O(1) recency, expiry heap, callbacks outside the lock
Rate limiter library: token bucket + sliding window behind one interface, per-key, bounded memory
Parking lot: pluggable pricing and allocation, no double allocation under contention
In-memory KV store with nested transactions, undo log and concurrent sessions
Pub-sub broker: bounded subscribers, acks, redelivery, dead letters, consumer groups
Job scheduler: heap + single dispatcher, recurring jobs, cancellation, graceful shutdown
Expense sharing: integer money, split strategies, debt simplification
Elevator controller: deterministic state machine, dispatch strategies, concurrent shell
Ticket booking: all-or-nothing seat holds, expiry, contention, idempotent confirm
In-memory file system: tree, atomic rename, walk, quota
Logger with decorator sinks and an async batching sink
Vending machine: state pattern, change-making, payment strategy
Order book / matching engine with price-time priority and invariants
Inventory and library reservations: two-phase holds, idempotency, waitlist
Resilient HTTP client: retry, budget, circuit breaker, bulkhead
URL shortener with pluggable ID generation and stores
STRETCH: leaderboard with O(log n) updates, rank and top-k
STRETCH: consistent-hashing cache client with lazy migration

outcomes.text: Run a timed machine-coding attempt: clarify and pin down requirements, state invariants out loud, hit stage checkpoints, and finish with a concurrency walk-through.
Choose data structures that give the required complexity (map + intrusive list, heaps with back-indices, undo logs, tick-driven state machines) and show the scale test that proves it.
Make a component safe for concurrent use under go test -race: state ownership, lock granularity and lock ordering, no user code under a lock, and invariants that a stress test can check.
Inject time (clocks, timers, ticks) so that every stage is testable without sleeping, including exact boundaries.
Land mid-interview requirement changes as additions (options, strategy interfaces, new methods) rather than rewrites of stage-1 code.
Design for lifecycle: bounded queues and memory, backpressure policies, graceful shutdown, panic containment and goroutine-leak freedom.
Model money, retries and duplicates correctly: integer minor units, deterministic rounding, idempotency keys, at-least-once delivery with dedupe.

Score your own code and a peer's against the machine-coding rubric (extensibility, concurrency safety, clean interfaces, tests, time management) and name the change that moves each dimension up a level.
Choose and defend a data model before coding (tree vs flat map, state pattern vs enum, sorted levels vs heap) and implement atomic tree operations with correct path handling.
Compose decorators and sinks with an explicit backpressure policy, failure isolation and a bounded graceful shutdown.
Implement the State pattern with an explicit transition table, reject invalid events, and make change correctly with finite coin stock.
Implement a price-time-priority matching engine with integer money, executable invariants and a differential test against a reference model.
Design reservations: reserve then commit or release with lazy expiry, all-or-nothing multi-item holds without deadlock, idempotency keys and a fair waitlist.
Build a resilient HTTP client: retry only what is safe, jittered backoff, retry budgets, circuit breaker, bulkhead and deadlines.
Design pluggable components with small consumer-side interfaces and shared contract tests.
Run a 90-minute machine-coding round: time budget with checkpoints, staged requirements, a deliberate concurrency pass and a spoken five-part concurrency note.
Choose an order-statistic structure for leaderboard top-k, rank and neighbours, and shard and merge top-k.
Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes, replication, bounded loads and lazy migration on membership change.
